This document describes how we map the checklist data to Darwin Core.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

Load libraries:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)
library(readxl)
library(digest)
```

# Read source data

The source data is maintained as an Excel file elsewhere. It is manually copied to this repository.

Read source data:
 
```{r}
raw_data <- read_excel(path = here("data", "raw", "checklist.xlsx")) 
```

Preview raw data:

```{r}
glimpse(raw_data)
```

# Create version 2.0

```{r}
input_data <- raw_data %>% clean_names()
```



```{r}
input_data <- input_data |>
  mutate(`taxonID hash` = vdigest(taxon, algo = "md5"),
         `scientific name` = taxon,
         kingdom = "Plantae",
         phylum = NA_character_,
         class = NA_character_ ,
         order = NA_character_ ,
         genus = NA_character_,
         `nomenclatural code` = "ICN",
         `country code` = "BE",
         `presence Flanders` = case_when(presence_fl == "X" ~ "TRUE", .default = "FALSE"),
         `presence Wallonia` = case_when(presence_wa == "X" ~ "TRUE", .default = "FALSE"),
         `presence Brussels` = case_when(presence_br == "X" ~ "TRUE", .default = "FALSE"),
         `occurrence status` = case_when(d_n == "Nat." | 
                                           d_n == "Cas." | 
                                           d_n == "Cas.?" | 
                                           d_n == "Nat.?" | 
                                           d_n == "Inv." ~ "present",
                                         .default = as.character(d_n)),
         `establishment means` = "introduced",
         `degree of establishment` = case_when(
           d_n == "Nat." | d_n == "Nat.?" ~ "established",
           d_n == "Cas."| d_n == "Cas.?" ~ "casual",
           d_n == "Inv." ~ "invasive",
           .default = as.character(d_n)),
         `introduction pathway 1` = NA_character_,
         `introduction pathway 2` = NA_character_,
         `introduction pathway 3` = NA_character_,
         `date of first observation` = 
         )
         
         
```





To link taxa with information in the extension(s), each taxon needs a unique and relatively stable `taxonID`. Here we create one in the form of `dataset_shortname:taxon:hash`, where `hash` is unique code based on scientific name (not kingdom).

```{r}
# Vectorize the digest function (The digest() function isn't vectorized. So if you pass in a vector, you get one value for the whole vector rather than a digest for each element of the vector):
vdigest <- Vectorize(digest)

input_data <-
  raw_data |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(taxon_id = vdigest(taxon, algo = "md5"))
```
